Oppelt et al. [@oppelt2018model] also measured the TNFα response of HepG2 cells under diclofenac
(DCF). Which rate constants does DCF change? The publication selected differences by an L1 scan and
a likelihood ratio test [@steiert2016l1]. This chapter repeats the scan and answers the same
question with spike-and-slab random effects. Model: the reduced model of
[Profile likelihood](guide-profiles.html); random effects and `em()`:
[Nonlinear mixed-effects models](guide-nlme.html). `dcf.R` computed the fits; the chapter loads
them.

The second part lists the sparse random-effect distributions and what their fits report;
derivations: [Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html).

## Data and model

TNFα-stimulated cells of the first blot scale, without (`TNF_none`) and with DCF (`TNF_DCF`).

```{r dcfdata}
```

With DCF an estimated rate constant $k$ becomes $\log k + \Delta_k$. `insert()` with
`x ~ 1 + (1 | gr(compound, dist = spikeSlab()))` writes each $\Delta_k$ as a random effect
`eta_<k>_DCF`, 0 without compound; the L1 scan treats the same symbols as parameters. 24
differences, as in the publication:

```{r dcfmodel, results = "hide"}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# the fixed values of the reduced model on the parameters of the DCF model
fixedDCF <- gauge[intersect(names(gauge), getParameters(prdDCF))]
changesDCF <- unique(na.omit(unlist(randomEffects(pDCF)$etas)))
# the prediction of both conditions at `pars`, the changes not in `pars` at 0, as a data frame
predictionOf <- function(prd, pars, changes) {
  off <- setdiff(changes, names(pars))
  data <- as.data.frame(dataDCF)
  times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, max(data$time), length.out = 200), data$time)))
  as.data.frame(prd(times, pars, fixed = c(fixedDCF, setNames(numeric(length(off)), off))))
}
dataFrameDCF <- as.data.frame(dataDCF)
onceDCF <- names(which(tapply(dataFrameDCF$time, dataFrameDCF$name, function(t) length(unique(t))) == 1L))
# against the data, each observable up to the last time it was measured, without those measured once
fitPlot <- function(prd, pars, changes) {
  pred <- predictionOf(prd, pars, changes)
  data <- dataFrameDCF[!dataFrameDCF$name %in% onceDCF, ]
  last <- tapply(data$time, data$name, max)
  pred <- pred[pred$name %in% names(last), ]
  pred <- pred[pred$time <= last[as.character(pred$name)], ]
  ggplot2::ggplot(data, ggplot2::aes(time, value, color = condition)) +
    ggplot2::geom_line(data = pred) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(ggplot2::aes(ymin = value - sigma, ymax = value + sigma), width = 0,
                           na.rm = TRUE) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.2) +
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ name, scales = "free") +
    scale_color_dMod2() +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "time [min]", y = "log signal", color = NULL) +
    theme_dMod2()
}
# the observables measured at one time: data and prediction per condition
fitOnce <- function(prd, pars, changes) {
  pred <- predictionOf(prd, pars, changes)
  data <- dataFrameDCF[dataFrameDCF$name %in% onceDCF, c("name", "time", "condition", "value", "sigma")]
  pred <- unique(merge(pred[pred$name %in% onceDCF, c("name", "time", "condition", "value")],
                       unique(data[c("name", "time")])))
  names(pred)[names(pred) == "value"] <- "prediction"
  out <- merge(pred, data)
  out[c("prediction", "value", "sigma")] <- lapply(out[c("prediction", "value", "sigma")], round, 2)
  out
}
```

## L1 scan

The penalty $\lambda \sum_k \lvert \Delta_k \rvert$ [@tibshirani1996regression; @steiert2016l1] is
added to $-2 \log L$; `trustL1()` sets differences exactly to 0
([L1 penalties](guide-optimization.html#l1-penalties)).

Four rate constants enter the data only as a product with a partner: `uptake` with
`act_Ikk_by_TNF`, `prod_Ikb` with `prod_mIkb_by_nNfk`, `build_RnaA20` with `build_A20`, and
`split_NfkIkb` with `eta_split_pNfkpIkb`. The reduced model fixes the four as gauge
([Symmetries](guide-symmetries.html)), so their differences are 0, and both methods share the
other 20 candidates. The publication penalized all 24 and set partners aside after the scan.

Each $\lambda$, 0 and 31 values from $10^{-2}$ to $10^4$ evenly on the log scale, runs 1000 starts
around the reduced fit, then starts from the best fits of the other $\lambda$ until none improves.
`dcf.R` runs the fits through `fitTasks()` ([Remote computing](guide-remote-computing.html)):

```{r dcfL1, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r dcfL1continue, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r}
dcfL1 <- stored("results/dcfL1.rds", "dcf.R", envir = new.env())
```

Waterfall of the best 200 values of $-2 \log L$ of the data, without the penalty, per $\lambda$,
the y axis shared within a row:

```{r, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 13}
objectiveL1 <- dcfL1$penalized
lambdaL1 <- sort(unique(objectiveL1$lambda))
# the best 200 fits per lambda, six lambdas per row, the y axis shared within a row
best200 <- function(x) {
  x <- head(x[order(x$value), ], 200)
  x$rank <- seq_len(nrow(x))
  x
}
waterL1 <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(lambdaL1), function(i)
  cbind(best200(objectiveL1[objectiveL1$lambda == lambdaL1[i], ]), row = (i - 1) %/% 6,
        col = (i - 1) %% 6, label = sprintf("lambda == %s", format(signif(lambdaL1[i], 3))))))
ggplot2::ggplot(waterL1, ggplot2::aes(rank, value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(color = converged), size = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::geom_text(data = unique(waterL1[c("row", "col", "label")]),
                     ggplot2::aes(x = 100, y = Inf, label = label), parse = TRUE, vjust = 1.4,
                     inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ggplot2::facet_grid(row ~ col, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "black", `FALSE` = dMod2_colors[2]),
                              labels = c(`TRUE` = "converged", `FALSE` = "not converged"),
                              name = NULL) +
  ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(expand = ggplot2::expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "fit rank", y = "-2 log L of the data") +
  theme_dMod2() +
  ggplot2::theme(strip.text = ggplot2::element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
penalizedAll <- dcfL1$penalized
penalizedAll$objective <- penalizedAll$value + penalizedAll$lambda * penalizedAll$L1
reachedL1 <- tapply(penalizedAll$objective, penalizedAll$lambda, function(v) sum(v < min(v) + 0.1))
waterText <- sprintf(paste(
  "Of at least %d fits per $\\lambda$, %d to %d reach the best penalized value within 0.1, a median %.0f; most",
  "others end at local optima or crawl and stop short."),
  min(table(penalizedAll$lambda)), min(reachedL1), max(reachedL1), median(reachedL1))
```

`r waterText`

Differences over $\lambda$ (Fig. 2a of the publication), in color those kept at the selected
$\lambda$ (dashed):

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
paths <- data.frame(lambda = rep(as.numeric(rownames(dcfL1$path)), ncol(dcfL1$path)),
                    difference = rep(sub("^eta_(.*)_DCF$", "\\1", colnames(dcfL1$path)),
                                     each = nrow(dcfL1$path)),
                    value = as.vector(dcfL1$path))
paths <- paths[paths$lambda > 0, ]
kept <- sub("^eta_(.*)_DCF$", "\\1", dcfL1$selected)
ggplot2::ggplot(paths, ggplot2::aes(lambda, value, group = difference)) +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = dcfL1$lambda, linetype = 2, color = "gray50") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = paths[!paths$difference %in% kept, ], color = "gray75") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = paths[paths$difference %in% kept, ], ggplot2::aes(color = difference)) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10(breaks = 10^(-2:4), labels = trimws(format(10^(-2:4), scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE))) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = expression(lambda), y = expression(Delta ~ "[log]"), color = NULL) +
  theme_dMod2()
```

Over $\lambda$ (Fig. 2b): $-2 \log L$ of the data (black), plus penalty (red, penalty gray), and
the number of nonzero differences:

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
scan <- dcfL1$scan[dcfL1$scan$lambda > 0, ]
curves <- rbind(data.frame(lambda = scan$lambda, value = scan$data, panel = "-2 log L", curve = "data"),
                data.frame(lambda = scan$lambda, value = scan$data + scan$penalty, panel = "-2 log L",
                           curve = "data + penalty"),
                data.frame(lambda = scan$lambda, value = scan$changes, panel = "nonzero differences",
                           curve = "count"))
ggplot2::ggplot(curves, ggplot2::aes(lambda, value)) +
  ggplot2::geom_ribbon(data = data.frame(lambda = scan$lambda, lo = scan$data,
                                         hi = scan$data + scan$penalty, panel = "-2 log L"),
                       ggplot2::aes(x = lambda, ymin = lo, ymax = hi), inherit.aes = FALSE,
                       fill = "gray85") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = dcfL1$lambda, linetype = 2, color = "gray50") +
  ggplot2::geom_line(ggplot2::aes(color = curve)) +
  ggplot2::scale_color_manual(values = c(data = "black", `data + penalty` = "#b2182b",
                                         count = "#2166ac"), guide = "none") +
  ggplot2::scale_x_log10(breaks = 10^(-2:4), labels = trimws(format(10^(-2:4), scientific = FALSE, drop0trailing = TRUE))) +
  ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ panel, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  ggplot2::labs(x = expression(lambda), y = NULL) +
  theme_dMod2()
```

The differences kept at each $\lambda$ are refitted without penalty, the others at 0, from the
best penalized fits and from 300 or more starts around the reduced fit. Selected is the largest
$\lambda$ whose refit the likelihood ratio test against all 20 candidates does not reject at
$p < 0.001$, as in the publication:

```{r dcfL1select, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
fullScan <- dcfL1$scan
rejected <- fullScan[!is.na(fullScan$p) & fullScan$p < 0.001 & fullScan$lambda > dcfL1$lambda, ][1, ]
selectedRow <- fullScan[fullScan$lambda == dcfL1$lambda, ]
scanText <- sprintf(paste(
  "The test rejects from $\\lambda = %.3g$ on, with %d differences and %.0f in $-2 \\log L$",
  "above the refit with all 20; the publication, with 24 candidates, rejected from $\\lambda = 10$",
  "on, with 11 differences and 34. Kept at $\\lambda = %.3g$ are %d differences: %s."),
  rejected$lambda, rejected$changes, rejected$refit - dcfL1$all$value, dcfL1$lambda,
  selectedRow$changes, enumerate(paste0("`", sort(kept), "`")))
```

`r scanText`

Of the 11 differences at $\lambda = 10$ the publication kept seven as independent
[@oppelt2018model]: it dropped `uptake`, `prod_Ikb`, `eta_int_pNfk` and `act_Nfk_by_Ikk` and took
`shuttle_RnaA20` in place of `build_A20`. The seven refitted alone, against the estimates and 95 %
intervals of the publication:

```{r}
publicationDCF <- dcfL1$publication
publicationDCF$refit <- unname(dcfL1$refitPublication$argument[paste0("eta_", publicationDCF$rate, "_DCF")])
publicationDCF
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
inside <- with(publicationDCF, refit >= lower & refit <= upper)
candidates <- ncol(dcfL1$path)
inSelected <- all(paste0("eta_", publicationDCF$rate, "_DCF") %in% dcfL1$selected)
publicationText <- sprintf(paste(
  "%s lie in the intervals of the publication. Against the refit with all %d candidates the seven",
  "give %.0f more in $-2 \\log L$ with %d fewer parameters, $p = %.2f$.%s"),
  if (all(inside)) "All seven estimates" else sprintf("%d of the seven estimates, all but %s,",
    sum(inside), enumerate(sprintf("`%s` (%.2f)", publicationDCF$rate[!inside], publicationDCF$refit[!inside]))),
  candidates, dcfL1$refitPublication$value - dcfL1$all$value, candidates - nrow(publicationDCF),
  pchisq(dcfL1$refitPublication$value - dcfL1$all$value, candidates - nrow(publicationDCF), lower.tail = FALSE),
  if (!inSelected) "" else sprintf(paste(
    " All seven are among the %d kept by the scan, against which they give %.0f more with %d fewer",
    "parameters, $p = %.2f$."), length(dcfL1$selected),
    dcfL1$refitPublication$value - dcfL1$refitSelected$value, length(dcfL1$selected) - nrow(publicationDCF),
    pchisq(dcfL1$refitPublication$value - dcfL1$refitSelected$value,
           length(dcfL1$selected) - nrow(publicationDCF), lower.tail = FALSE)))
```

## Spike and slab

With $\theta_k$ the log rate constant $k$, cells with DCF use $\theta_k + \Delta_k$. The
spike-and-slab distribution [@mitchell1988bayesian; @george1993variable] of a difference is

$$p(\Delta_k) = (1 - \rho)\, \delta(\Delta_k) + \rho\, \mathcal{N}(\Delta_k;\, 0, \tau^2),$$

with inclusion probability $\rho$ (`prob_compound`) and slab standard deviation $\tau$
(`tau_compound`, log scale). `em()` estimates $\theta$, $\rho$ and $\tau$ from the likelihood with
the differences integrated out, a sum over subsets
([Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal)).
$p_0 = \Pr(\Delta_k = 0 \mid y)$ is the posterior spike probability.

The candidates are the same 20 as in the L1 scan; with both partners of a product as candidates,
neither would reach a probability of one half. `dcf.R` runs 1000 starts of `msem()` around the
reduced fit, then 200 around the best. Waterfall of the 200:

```{r dcfspikeslab, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r dcfspikeslabmore, eval = FALSE}
```

```{r, fig.height = 3.5}
dcfSS <- stored("results/dcf.rds", "dcf.R", envir = new.env())
plotValues(dcfSS, round == 2)
dcfSS$argument[c("prob_compound", "tau_compound")]
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
first <- dcfSS$multistart[dcfSS$multistart$round == 1, ]
second <- dcfSS$multistart[dcfSS$multistart$round == 2, ]
plateau <- c(sum(first$value < dcfSS$value + 0.1), sum(second$value < dcfSS$value + 0.1))
hyperText <- sprintf(
  "%d of the %d starts around the reduced fit and %d of the %d around the best end within 0.1 of the best value. With $\\rho = %.2f$ a difference is expected for %.0f of the 20 rate constants; with $\\tau = %.2f$ a difference is typically a factor of %.1f.",
  plateau[1], nrow(first), plateau[2], nrow(second), dcfSS$argument[["prob_compound"]],
  20 * dcfSS$argument[["prob_compound"]], dcfSS$argument[["tau_compound"]],
  exp(dcfSS$argument[["tau_compound"]]))
```

`r hyperText` Probability of a difference, $1 - p_0$, labeled with the difference in the most
probable subset; crosses mark the seven of the publication:

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 5}
probability <- dcfSS$random[, c("eta", "mode", "p0")]
probability$eta <- factor(probability$eta, levels = rev(probability$eta))
probability$publication <- probability$eta %in% publicationDCF$rate
ggplot2::ggplot(probability, ggplot2::aes(1 - p0, eta)) +
  ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#2166ac") +
  ggplot2::geom_vline(xintercept = 0.5, linetype = 2, color = "gray50") +
  ggplot2::geom_text(data = probability[probability$mode != 0, ],
                     ggplot2::aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", mode)), hjust = -0.2, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = probability[probability$publication, ], ggplot2::aes(x = -0.04),
                      shape = 4, size = 2.5) +
  ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.06, 1.15), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.25)) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "probability of a difference", y = NULL) +
  theme_dMod2()
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
ssSet <- as.character(probability$eta[probability$mode != 0])
sharedSS <- intersect(ssSet, publicationDCF$rate)
sameSign <- all(sign(dcfSS$random$mode[match(sharedSS, dcfSS$random$eta)]) ==
                sign(publicationDCF$value[match(sharedSS, publicationDCF$rate)]))
missing <- setdiff(publicationDCF$rate, ssSet)
extra <- setdiff(ssSet, publicationDCF$rate)
ssText <- sprintf(paste(
  "The most probable subset holds %d differences, %d of them among the seven of the publication,",
  if (sameSign) "with the same signs." else "not all with the same signs.", "%s%s",
  "Refitted without the slab, the subset gives %.0f more in $-2 \\log L$ than all 20 candidates,",
  "the seven of the publication %.0f."),
  length(ssSet), length(sharedSS),
  if (length(missing)) sprintf("Not in it: %s. ", enumerate(sprintf("`%s` ($p_0 = %.2f$)", missing,
    dcfSS$random$p0[match(missing, dcfSS$random$eta)]))) else "",
  if (length(extra)) sprintf("In addition: %s. ", enumerate(sprintf("`%s`", extra))) else "",
  dcfL1$refitSpikeSlab$value - dcfL1$all$value, dcfL1$refitPublication$value - dcfL1$all$value)
# the likelihood ratio test of the subset against the seven of the publication, where it lies in them
if (all(ssSet %in% publicationDCF$rate)) {
  gainPub <- dcfL1$refitSpikeSlab$value - dcfL1$refitPublication$value
  dfPub <- nrow(publicationDCF) - length(ssSet)
  ssText <- paste(ssText, sprintf(paste(
    "Against the seven, the subset gives %.2f more in $-2 \\log L$ with %d %s fewer, $p = %.2f$."),
    gainPub, dfPub, if (dfPub == 1L) "parameter" else "parameters",
    pchisq(gainPub, dfPub, lower.tail = FALSE)))
}
```

`r ssText` The 20 differences are exchangeable under the model: the nonzero ones against the slab
density $\rho\, \mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ (line), the count at 0 against the expected
$20 (1 - \rho)$ (bar). With `r length(ssSet)` nonzero differences the figure shows gross departures
from the slab, an outlier or separate clusters, but is no test of its shape:

```{r, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 3}
rho <- dcfSS$argument[["prob_compound"]]
tau <- dcfSS$argument[["tau_compound"]]
nonzero <- dcfSS$random$mode[dcfSS$random$mode != 0]
slab <- data.frame(x = seq(-4, 4, length.out = 401))
slab$density <- 20 * rho * dnorm(slab$x, 0, tau)
ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::geom_line(data = slab, ggplot2::aes(x, density)) +
  ggplot2::geom_rug(data = data.frame(x = nonzero), ggplot2::aes(x), sides = "b", linewidth = 0.8,
                    length = grid::unit(0.08, "npc")) +
  ggplot2::geom_segment(ggplot2::aes(x = 0, xend = 0, y = 0, yend = sum(dcfSS$random$mode == 0)),
                        linewidth = 2, color = dMod2_colors[2]) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(x = 0, y = 20 * (1 - rho)), shape = 4, size = 3) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = expression(Delta ~ "[log]"), y = "differences per unit") +
  theme_dMod2()
```

The model at the spike-and-slab estimates against the data:

```{r, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 8}
parsSS <- c(dcfSS$argument[setdiff(names(dcfSS$argument), c("prob_compound", "tau_compound"))],
            setNames(dcfSS$random$mode, paste0("eta_", dcfSS$random$eta, "_DCF")))
fitPlot(gDCF * xDCF * pSS, parsSS, unique(na.omit(unlist(randomEffects(pSS)$etas))))
fitOnce(gDCF * xDCF * pSS, parsSS, unique(na.omit(unlist(randomEffects(pSS)$etas))))
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# bias: the kept differences at the penalized estimates against their refit without penalty, and
# the spike-and-slab values against the refit of the same subset
keptNames <- dcfL1$selected
shrinkL1 <- abs(dcfL1$refitSelected$argument[keptNames]) - abs(dcfL1$penalizedSelected[keptNames])
ssNames <- paste0("eta_", ssSet, "_DCF")
shiftSS <- abs(dcfSS$random$mode[match(ssSet, dcfSS$random$eta)]) - abs(dcfL1$refitSpikeSlab$argument[ssNames])
ssInL1 <- all(ssNames %in% dcfL1$selected)
compareText <- sprintf(paste(
  "It needs one multistart, no scan over $\\lambda$ and no refits. The penalty shrinks every kept",
  "difference toward 0, at the selected $\\lambda$ by a median %.2f on the log scale against the",
  "refit without the penalty, more at larger $\\lambda$; the spike and slab leaves the size of a",
  "difference to the slab, and the spike-and-slab differences lie a median %.2f from the refit of",
  "the same subset.%s"),
  median(shrinkL1), median(abs(shiftSS)),
  if (!ssInL1) "" else sprintf(paste(
    " The most probable subset lies within the %d differences the scan keeps and fits the data",
    "not worse than they do, $p = %.2f$ for the %d others."), length(dcfL1$selected),
    pchisq(dcfL1$refitSpikeSlab$value - dcfL1$refitSelected$value,
           length(dcfL1$selected) - length(ssNames), lower.tail = FALSE),
    length(dcfL1$selected) - length(ssNames)))
```

## L1 scan and spike and slab

Both methods see the same data, model, prior and 20 candidates:

```{r, echo = FALSE}
allValue <- dcfL1$all$value
row <- function(method, set, value) data.frame(method = method, differences = length(set),
  `-2 log L` = round(value, 2), `p against all 20` = signif(pchisq(value - allValue, 20 - length(set),
  lower.tail = FALSE), 2), check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(rbind(row("L1 scan and test", dcfL1$selected, dcfL1$refitSelected$value),
                   row("spike and slab", ssNames, dcfL1$refitSpikeSlab$value),
                   row("publication", publicationDCF$rate, dcfL1$refitPublication$value),
                   row("all candidates", seq_len(20), allValue)))
```

The spike and slab is faster and free of shrinkage. `r compareText` The L1 scan
only tests subsets that are the penalized optimum at some $\lambda$; the spike and slab weighs every
subset ([Methods > Selection of deviations](methods-sparsity-priors.html#selection-of-deviations)).
The fit reports the most probable subset; the differences with $p_0 < 0.5$, the median probability
model, which predicts best under broad conditions [@barbieri2004optimal],
`r medianSS <- as.character(dcfSS$random$eta[dcfSS$random$p0 < 0.5]); if (setequal(medianSS, ssSet)) "are the same here" else sprintf("are %s here", enumerate(paste0("\x60", sort(medianSS), "\x60")))`.

```{r, include = FALSE}
seText <- if (is.null(tryCatch(vcov(dcfSS), error = function(e) NULL)))
  "has one group, too few for the empirical information, and the intervals are missing" else
  "the conditions without DCF and the prior complete the one group"
```

## Sparse random-effect distributions

`gr(group, dist = )` sets the random-effect distribution. Besides `normal()`, two give deviations
exactly zero unless the data need them:

| distribution | a deviation $\eta$ of a group | hyperparameters |
|---|---|---|
| `spikeSlab()` | $0$ with probability $1 - \rho$, else $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ | `prob_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |
| `dirichletProcess()` | cluster value: $0$ for the population cluster, else one $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$ draw | `concentration_<grouping>`, `tau_<grouping>` |

Hyperparameters are shared by the symbols of a term (`_1`, `_2`, ... for several terms of one
grouping) and estimated unless given, as in `spikeSlab(tau = 0.5)`. Normal and sparse random
effects of one grouping combine; `em(method = "focei")` fits all.

## Fitting sparse random effects

`em(method = "focei")` integrates sparse random effects by the Laplace approximation at the joint
mode of a group, exactly where possible, and by expectation consistent (EC) approximation where the
data link a Dirichlet-process effect to another factor or the subset sum exceeds the budget. Fixed
effects and hyperparameters move in one trust region. `fit$coupling` is `"expectationConsistent"`
if a group needed EC, else `NULL`. Methods:
[Methods > Approximate marginal](methods-sparsity-priors.html#approximate-marginal),
[Methods > Expectation consistent
approximation](methods-sparsity-priors.html#expectation-consistent-approximation) and
[Methods > Joint trust region](methods-sparsity-priors.html#joint-trust-region).

| entry of `control$sparseFit` | default | controls |
|---|---|---|
| `maxOuter` | `200` | joint trust-region iterations, all runs |
| `trustControl` | `rinit = 1`, `rmax = 10`, `ftol = 1e-10`, `mtol = 1e-5` | joint trust region, as `trust()` |

Other entries are an error. The DCF fit passes the `tolerances` of
[Setting up models](guide-model.html) in `trustControl`. A run stopping short of `mtol` restarts
while runs lower $-2 \log L$ by more than `mtol`. `msem()` perturbs concentrations and slab
standard deviations on log scale, probabilities on logit scale.

## Reported structure

The fit reports the most probable subset (spike and slab) or partition (Dirichlet process): spike
deviations exactly zero, slab deviations the posterior mean given the structure
([Methods > Reported structure](methods-sparsity-priors.html#reported-structure)).
`fit$random` has a row per group and random effect:

- `mode`, this value;
- `se`, posterior standard deviation over spike and slab;
- spike-and-slab and Dirichlet process: `cluster`, 0 for the population value, 1, 2, ... for
  deviating groups or clusters in group order, and `p0`, posterior probability of zero deviation;
- `data`, whether the random effect reaches data of the group, where some do not.

A sparse random effect reaching no data of the group rests at 0 with the prior standard deviation
and, for spike and slab, $p_0 = 1 - \rho$. `fit$slab` lists probabilities, concentrations and slab
standard deviations, each with term symbols, estimate and whether fixed.

## Standard errors

With spike-and-slab random effects `fit$hessian` is `NULL`; `vcov()` inverts `fit$information`,
the empirical information of the group scores plus the expected information of the conditions
without random effects and the priors (`hessian = "expected"`). It needs more groups than
parameters, or those terms for the other directions; otherwise `vcov()` is an error and standard
errors are `NA`. `fit$information` is not a Hessian of the marginal and does not detect saddle
points. The DCF fit `r seText`. `dirichletProcess()` fits have neither;
`confint(method = "profile")` gives intervals.
Details: [Methods > Standard errors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#standard-errors).

## Dirichlet-process random effects

With `gr(group, dist = dirichletProcess())` groups and population value form clusters; the
concentration $\alpha$ sets how readily a group opens a new one. The population cluster has
deviation zero, every other cluster one common deviation from $\mathcal{N}(0, \tau^2)$. $\alpha$
and $\tau$ are estimated by marginal maximum likelihood in one fit.

`method = "focei"` sums exactly over partitions of up to 14 groups. `method = "saem"` draws
partitions, allows normal but no other sparse random effects alongside, and reports the most
frequent partition of the last `window` iterations after burn-in, with standard error `valueSE` of
$-2 \log L$. `control$saem$particles` sets the importance-sampling particles, default 500;
`converged` says whether burn-in ended by the drift test. An SAEM fit has no gradient, Hessian or
empirical information. Details:
[Methods > Sparsity priors](methods-sparsity-priors.html#dirichlet-process-random-effects).

Reference: `randomEffects()`, `spikeSlab()`, `dirichletProcess()`, `em()`, `msem()`,
`plotValues()`, `plotTrace()`, `plotRandomEffects()`, `plotPars()`
